title: Plan: Math utilities module (swephlib.c partial)
description:
Port the pure-math portion of swephlib.c (~1500 lines). All stateless pure functions.

## Functions to port

**Coordinate transforms (swephlib.c:279-420):**
| C function | Rust signature idea | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| `swi_coortrf(xpo, xpn, eps)` | `rotate_x(pos: [f64;3], eps: f64) -> [f64;3]` | Rotation about x-axis by angle ε. Ecliptic↔equatorial. |
| `swi_coortrf2(xpo, xpn, sineps, coseps)` | `rotate_x_sincos(pos, sin_eps, cos_eps)` | Same but precomputed sin/cos |
| `swi_cartpol(x, l)` | `cartesian_to_polar(xyz: [f64;3]) -> (lon, lat, dist)` | atan2(y,x), atan(z/rxy) |
| `swi_polcart(l, x)` | `polar_to_cartesian(lon, lat, dist) -> [f64;3]` | Inverse |
| `swi_cartpol_sp(x, l)` | `cartesian_to_polar_with_velocity(xv: [f64;6]) -> [f64;6]` | Includes Jacobian for velocity transform |
| `swi_polcart_sp(l, x)` | `polar_to_cartesian_with_velocity(lv: [f64;6]) -> [f64;6]` | Inverse with velocity |

**Angle normalization (swephlib.c + sweph.c):**
- `swe_degnorm(x)` → `normalize_degrees(x) -> f64` — result in [0, 360)
- `swe_radnorm(x)` → `normalize_radians(x) -> f64` — result in [0, 2π)
- `swe_deg_midp(x1, x0)` → `midpoint_degrees(a, b) -> f64` — shortest arc midpoint
- `swe_difdeg2n(p1, p2)` → `diff_degrees(a, b) -> f64` — result in [-180, 180)
- Plus the centisecond variants (csnorm, difcsn, difcs2n) — maybe skip or make optional

**Chebyshev evaluation (swephlib.c):**
- `swi_echeb(t, coef, ncf)` → `chebyshev_eval(t: f64, coeffs: &[f64]) -> f64` — Clenshaw recurrence for T_n(t)
- `swi_edcheb(t, coef, ncf)` → `chebyshev_deriv(t: f64, coeffs: &[f64]) -> f64` — derivative via modified Chebyshev

**Degree splitting:**
- `swe_split_deg(ddeg, roundflag, ...)` → `split_degrees(deg: f64, flags: SplitFlags) -> DegreeParts`

**Other math (swephlib.c):**
- `swe_d2l(x)` — double to i32 with rounding
- `swi_mod2PI(x)` — normalize to [0, 2π)
- `swi_nterm_pol(t, coeffs, n)` — evaluate polynomial Σ c_i × t^i

## Key algorithm: Chebyshev Clenshaw recurrence (from catalogue-internal §4.1)
```
Position: pc[0]=1, pc[1]=t; for i=2..ncf: pc[i] = 2t×pc[i-1] − pc[i-2]; result = Σ pc[j]×coeff[j]
Velocity: vc[0]=0, vc[1]=1, vc[2]=4t; for i=3..ncf: vc[i] = 2t×vc[i-1] + 2×pc[i-1] − vc[i-2]
```

## Key algorithm: Cartesian→Polar with velocity (Jacobian)
The velocity transform uses the Jacobian of the (x,y,z)→(lon,lat,r) mapping. This is where numerical precision matters — small r_xy values can cause division issues.

## Testing
- Coordinate transforms: round-trip property (cart→pol→cart = identity within ε)
- Chebyshev: evaluate known polynomials (T_0=1, T_1=t, T_2=2t²-1) and verify
- Angle normalization: wrap-around edge cases, negative inputs, values near 360/2π boundaries
- Compare all outputs against C for specific inputs

## C source reference
- swephlib.c:279-420 — coordinate transforms
- swephlib.c:314-420 — polar conversions with velocity
- swephlib.c Chebyshev functions (search for swi_echeb)

## Dependencies
- Phase 0 (types, constants)

acceptance_criteria.text: All 23 functions implemented in src/math.rs with correct visibility (pub for swe_* equivalents, pub(crate) for swi_* equivalents)
DegreeParts struct added to src/types.rs, TWOPI constant added to src/constants.rs
Angle normalization uses % (fmod), not rem_euclid, with near-zero guard matching C exactly
Chebyshev evaluation uses reverse iterator to avoid bounds-check overhead in tight loops
cartesian_to_polar_with_speed handles rxy→0 polar singularity per C code (zero-position and zero-speed branches)
Golden test C generator covers all function groups with curated edge-case vectors
Golden tests pass bitwise-exact (assert_f64_exact) for all pure-math functions
cargo test passes (unit tests + golden tests)
Nakshatra support in split_degrees deferred (ignored if flag passed) — documented for swisseph-rs/9

decisions.decision: swi_* functions made pub instead of pub(crate)
decisions.rationale: Integration tests in tests/golden/ cannot access pub(crate) items. The C library exposes these via swephlib.h, so pub matches the actual C visibility. The swi_ prefix naming convention still signals internal use.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Move golden tests for internal functions into #[cfg(test)] mod in math.rs — would split test code across two files and require duplicating the JSON loader

execution_record:
Diverged from plan on visibility: swi_* functions changed from pub(crate) to pub because integration tests (tests/golden/) can't access pub(crate) items. The C library exposes these via swephlib.h anyway — swi_ prefix is a naming convention, not access control.

Discovered serde_json 1-ULP float parsing bug for certain decimal strings (e.g., 0.93027401411547206). Fixed by enabling the float_roundtrip feature in Cargo.toml.

3 commits: db40c48 (implementation + unit tests), e4f3c2f (golden tests + C generator), 7192a42 (visibility fix).

Codex adversarial review (verdict: needs-attention → assessed as approve):

Structural review (sutra): risk 0.677, no constraint violations, convention violations are false positives (test helpers in tests/ flagged as should-be-in-src).

1. [high → out of scope] AsteroidId overflow in Body::to_raw_id: valid concern but applies to the phase-0 scaffold types, not swisseph-rs/3's math module changes. Already fixed by swisseph-rs/17 (commit 07077b8, range-validated newtypes). Codex diffed 8035663..HEAD which includes later commits beyond this task's scope.

The math port itself — all 23 functions, golden tests, C generator — reviewed clean. Codex verified cargo test passes. No correctness issues found in the coordinate transforms, Chebyshev evaluation, angle normalization, or split_degrees implementation."
